h2: Pool Repair Seminyak – Leaks, Tiles & Pipework for Villas
intro: If your villa pool in Petitenget or Oberoi is losing water overnight, shedding mosaic pieces, or showing tired grout lines, Pool Repair Seminyak is where you want a technician who understands how old local infrastructure actually behaves. Most pools here are 15–20 years old, and with dense plots plus shared walls, even a small pipe leak can become urgent fast. Send photos on WhatsApp and I'll tell you what needs fixing first.

sections.h3: Why Seminyak Pools Need Attention Sooner
sections.text: Dense villa clusters in Basangkasa and Batu Belig mean tight access, shared drainage, and older pipework running under concrete slabs. When heavy rain floods the lanes, septic systems overload and pump rooms get waterlogged. High-occupancy rentals add pressure: a blocked mixer or a slow drip behind a tile line becomes a guest complaint within hours. I work around check-in schedules so repairs land between stays, not during them.

sections.h3: What I Fix – and What to Tackle First
sections.text: Typical jobs include leak detection for pools quietly losing litres overnight, replacing loose mosaic tiles before they pull their neighbours out, re-grouting worn coping lines, and tracing pipe leaks in pump rooms that are hard to reach on small plots. With many villas now 15–25 years old, I help you prioritise: fix the active leak first, then address cosmetic grout and tile wear so you're not paying twice. A quote comes from photos sent on WhatsApp.

A few clear shots save everyone time. Photograph the affected area at ground level and from above, any visible damp patches on adjacent walls, the pump room if accessible, and the waterline where tiles look lifted. If the pool is dropping level over a day or two, note the starting and ending mark. Send all of it on WhatsApp with your villa name and neighbourhood – Petitenget, Oberoi, Drupadi – and I'll come back with what needs doing and a rough scope.

In Seminyak's humid climate, grout degrades faster than in drier regions, and salt-air near Batu Belig accelerates corrosion on fittings. Check tile lines monthly for hollow spots; press gently and listen. Keep the skimmer clean so debris doesn't abrade the interior surface. After heavy rain, inspect the pump room for standing water and confirm the drain still flows. Small attention now means fewer emergency calls between guest stays.

faq.q: How do you find a leak without draining the whole pool?
faq.a: I use pressure testing on isolated pipe sections and visual dye checks at suspect joints. Most diagnostics don't require emptying the pool.

faq.q: Can you work around my guests' schedule?
faq.a: Yes – I plan visits between check-ins or during quiet hours. Just let me know the occupancy window when you message on WhatsApp.

faq.q: Do you handle both the plumbing side and the cosmetic tile and grout work?
faq.a: Both. If a loose mosaic is hiding a small pipe crack, I fix the pipe first, then reset the tiles and re-grout so the finish looks right again.
